items.title: Avakian George — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: That’s the first time that I went down to Greenwich Village, for example, and heard the band at Nick’s with Condon, Freeman, Pee Wee Russell, and so forth, Dave Tough, and then on 52nd Street.

ctx.x: It exists if they’ll seek it out, but there’s no real way in which they can do it, it seems to me, for these reasons. First of all, radio – which every young person gets hooked on – and now MTV pays no attention to jazz. They’re not going to stumble into Jazz 88 on FM unless it’s an accident that grabs them, because they’re too busy turning the dial, and they can hear every other kind of popular music. The other thing is, where do they get to hear it? They can’t go into the clubs. Not that I was able to go into a…

Then, when I was old enough to go out by myself, I didn’t really start doing it, because of the kind of family that I was in, until I was college age. That’s the first time that I went down to Greenwich Village, for example, and heard the band at Nick’s with Condon, Freeman, Pee Wee Russell, and so forth, Dave Tough, and then on 52nd Street. So I didn’t start doing that until I was 18. And then kids don’t have any guidance in terms of their own peers, their older brothers and sisters, just as I had guidance from…

That’s probably it, isn’t it, that the parents of today’s generation, did not – at least your children and my children had the opportunity to be exposed to the music, because even if they didn’t . . .
